title: Matrix Cells in Distance Order
description:
You are given four integers `rows`, `cols`, `rCenter`, and `cCenter` describing a `rows x cols` matrix and a center cell `(rCenter, cCenter)`.

Return a 2D array containing the `[r, c]` coordinates of every cell in the matrix, ordered by increasing **Manhattan distance** `|r - rCenter| + |c - cCenter|` from `(rCenter, cCenter)`. If two cells have the same Manhattan distance, order them by smaller row `r`, and if rows are equal, by smaller column `c`.
hints: The maximum possible Manhattan distance from (rCenter, cCenter) is at most (rows - 1) + (cols - 1).

Bucket all coordinates by their Manhattan distance while scanning r from 0 to rows - 1 and c from 0 to cols - 1; each bucket automatically respects the (r, c) tie-breaking order in O(rows * cols) time.

examples.explanation: From (0, 0) in a 1x2 grid, distances are 0 at (0, 0) and 1 at (0, 1).
From (0, 1) in a 2x2 grid, (0, 1) has distance 0, (0, 0) and (1, 1) have distance 1 (ordered by row), and (1, 0) has distance 2.
From (1, 2) in a 2x3 grid, cells are grouped by Manhattan shells 0, 1, 2, 3 with row-major tie-breaking.
